_readme:
Claims about jurisdictions outside Portugal. These sit in a separate file from facts.json for two reasons. First, facts.json is keyed by the bare figure and feeds GEO scoring, and several of these claims turn on numbers that mean something else elsewhere in this corpus (10% is a Spanish ITP band here and the CPCV deposit convention on forty other pages), so registering them there would hand unrelated articles a provenance they have not earned. Second, and the actual point: nobody on this project monitors HMRC, the IRS, the Spanish autonomous communities or Greek ENFIA the way Portuguese law is followed here. These figures will go out of date without anyone noticing. Each carries a reviewBy date; npm run facts:review fails once one is overdue, which is the whole mechanism. Reviewing means re-reading the primary source and either moving the dates forward or correcting every file the claim names.

Why this file matters more here than on most sites: the two worst-scoring collections in this corpus, segments (13 pages) and compare (14 pages), exist entirely to describe foreign jurisdictions. That is 27 of 141 pages whose central claims nobody here watches. This is a seed set covering the claims that are load-bearing today; the rewrite waves are expected to add to it, because a segment page rewritten to hold what the buyer's OWN country does to them is by definition a page built on an external claim.

claims.claim: The UK-Portugal double taxation convention dates from 1968 and relieves double taxation by the credit method, not by exemption, so Portuguese tax paid on Portuguese-source income is credited against the UK bill rather than removing the UK charge
claims.source: UK/Portugal Double Taxation Convention 1968, HMRC Double Taxation Relief manual

claims.claim: Under the 1968 convention, UK government-service pensions remain taxable only in the UK, unlike other occupational and state pensions which move to the residence country
claims.source: UK/Portugal Double Taxation Convention 1968, government service article

claims.claim: The UK replaced the remittance basis with the four-year foreign income and gains regime from April 2025, which changes the arithmetic for returners and for new UK arrivals holding Portuguese property
claims.source: UK Finance Act provisions on the foreign income and gains regime, HMRC guidance

claims.claim: The United States taxes its citizens on worldwide income regardless of residence, so a US citizen who becomes Portuguese tax resident continues to file a US return on Portuguese rental income and gains
claims.source: US Internal Revenue Code; IRS Publication 54

claims.claim: A US person must file an FBAR once the aggregate value of foreign financial accounts exceeds USD 10,000 at any point in the calendar year, a threshold a Portuguese purchase account crosses immediately
claims.source: FinCEN Form 114 instructions; 31 CFR 1010.350

claims.claim: Form 8938 reporting under FATCA applies in addition to the FBAR, at higher and residence-dependent thresholds, and directly held foreign real estate is not itself a specified foreign financial asset
claims.source: IRS Form 8938 instructions; IRC section 6038D

claims.claim: A section 1031 like-kind exchange cannot defer gain between US and non-US real property, so a US owner cannot roll a Portuguese sale into a US purchase tax-deferred
claims.source: IRC section 1031(h)

claims.claim: Germany relieves foreign rental income by exemption with progression rather than by credit, so exempt Portuguese income still raises the German rate applied to the rest of the taxpayer's income
claims.source: German Einkommensteuergesetz section 32b; Germany-Portugal double taxation treaty

claims.claim: Canada taxes residents on worldwide income and applies a deemed disposition on ceasing residence, so the timing of a move interacts with a Portuguese purchase differently from the US citizenship-based rule
claims.source: Canadian Income Tax Act section 128.1; CRA guidance on emigrants

claims.claim: Spanish transfer tax on resale property (ITP) is set by each autonomous community rather than nationally, so a single Spain-wide rate cannot be quoted against a single Portuguese one
claims.source: Spanish Ley del ITP y AJD; autonomous community tax schedules

claims.claim: Italian purchase taxation turns on registration tax computed from cadastral value rather than price for private resale purchases, which makes headline-rate comparison with Portuguese IMT misleading
claims.source: Italian Testo Unico dell'imposta di registro (DPR 131/1986); Agenzia delle Entrate guidance

claims.claim: Greece levies ENFIA as its recurring property tax, structured as a main tax per square metre plus a supplementary charge on higher-value holdings, which is not comparable line-for-line with Portuguese IMI plus AIMI
claims.source: Greek Law 4223/2013 on ENFIA; AADE guidance

claims.claim: US income tax treaties contain a saving clause under which the United States reserves the right to tax its own citizens and residents as if the treaty had not entered into force, subject to stated exceptions, so a US citizen becoming Portuguese tax resident continues to file in the United States
claims.source: US Model Income Tax Convention, saving clause article; IRS Publication 901

claims.claim: The US foreign tax credit is available for foreign income taxes, so Portuguese tax on rental income and gains can be creditable while IMT, IMI, AIMI and stamp duty, being transfer and property taxes, are not
claims.source: IRC sections 901 and 903; IRS Publication 514

claims.claim: Since the end of free movement, British citizens are third-country nationals in the Schengen area and limited to 90 days of presence in any rolling 180-day period, counted across all Schengen states with entry and exit days counting in full
claims.source: Regulation (EU) 2016/399, Schengen Borders Code, article 6

claims.claim: The EU Entry/Exit System registers third-country nationals' entries and exits electronically in place of manual passport stamping, so the 90/180 calculation is held as a record rather than reconstructed
claims.source: Regulation (EU) 2017/2226 establishing the Entry/Exit System

claims.claim: French tax residents are assessed to the impot sur la fortune immobiliere on worldwide real estate, so a Portuguese property enters the French wealth-tax base while a non-resident is assessed on French property only
claims.source: Code general des impots, articles 964 and following

claims.claim: Germany taxes inheritance and gift on a worldwide basis where the deceased or the heir is German-resident, has concluded inheritance tax treaties with only a small number of states not including Portugal, and relieves double taxation by crediting foreign inheritance tax actually paid
claims.source: Erbschaftsteuer- und Schenkungsteuergesetz, sections 2 and 21; German Federal Ministry of Finance list of inheritance tax treaties

claims.claim: Canadian residents must file Form T1135 where the total cost amount of specified foreign property exceeds CAD 100,000, and property held primarily for personal use and enjoyment is excluded from that definition, so use rather than value decides whether a foreign home is reportable
claims.source: Canadian Income Tax Act section 233.3; CRA Form T1135 instructions

claims.claim: On ceasing Canadian residence, most property is deemed disposed of at fair market value, and foreign real property falls within that deemed disposition, so a Portuguese house can crystallise a Canadian gain on departure
claims.source: Canadian Income Tax Act section 128.1(4); CRA guidance for emigrants

claims.claim: The United Arab Emirates levies no personal income tax on individuals, so a UAE-resident individual has no home income tax liability against which Portuguese tax on rent or gains could be credited
claims.source: UAE federal tax legislation; UAE Ministry of Finance guidance on the scope of corporate tax and the absence of personal income tax
